title: Intracellular complement factor H protects neurons during CNS inflammation.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Downloaded GSE332759_gene_counts.txt.gz (3.7 MB, a featureCounts gene-count table) from GEO: 16 sample columns (4 biological replicates x wild-type/Cfh knockout x control/glutamate) and about 43,600 mouse Ensembl gene rows (GRCm38 release 79). GEO search found no human single-nucleus RNA-seq series linked to this paper; PubMed elink (PMID 42686909) returned no GEO/SRA links; Europe PMC has no full text, supplement or text-mined accessions.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The human single-nucleus RNA-seq (snRNA-seq) of retinal ganglion cells from multiple sclerosis and control donors, and its donor/nucleus counts, come only from the abstract; the Nature page is paywalled, so I could not read the data availability statement or learn where that data sits (possibly controlled access or not yet deposited).

a1_downloadable.note: The mouse bulk count table downloads from GEO (checked). The human single-nucleus data, the only part that could support ML, was not found in GEO, and the paywalled paper's data statement could not be read.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The bulk table has only genotype/treatment, encoded in sample names (checked). A per-cell-type 'resilience' label would have to be built from donor-level cell-loss estimates that aren't public.

a3_inputs_present.note: Gene counts are present for all 16 bulk samples (checked).

a4_units_stated.note: Raw read counts from featureCounts, gene-level, stated in the file header (checked).

a5_enough_rows.note: 16 bulk RNA-seq samples (checked); far below the ~400 minimum for classification. Human donor count unknown.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: 16 samples match the GEO series description (checked); paper's own counts not readable.

a8_label_provenance.note: Genotype and treatment are experimental design, not model outputs.

honest_claim_h3: With 16 mouse culture samples, no model can claim anything beyond a differential-expression result for Cfh knockout under glutamate stress.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use gene expression of retinal neuron subtypes to predict which subtypes survive inflammation in multiple sclerosis.
plain_idea.train_on: Per-nucleus gene expression from human retinal ganglion cells (donor and nucleus counts unknown, data not found publicly); the public mouse table has only 16 bulk samples.
plain_idea.predict: How resilient each neuron subtype is, measured as relative cell loss in multiple sclerosis versus control donor retinas.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Neurologists and neuroprotection labs would learn which genes besides CFH mark neurons that resist inflammatory damage.

ml_idea: Predict neuron-subtype resilience to inflammation from snRNA-seq (single-nucleus RNA sequencing) profiles; not feasible because the human data is not publicly located and the public mouse data is 16 bulk samples.

effort.compute_note: Not estimated; project rejected at Part A.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Find the human snRNA-seq accession in the paper's data availability statement; if it is controlled access or absent, the project is dead (it already is on public data).

verdict_reason: A mechanistic biology paper: the only public data is a 16-sample mouse bulk RNA-seq knockout experiment (GSE332759, checked), too small for ML (A5). The human single-nucleus data that could support a resilience model was not found in any public repository (A1), and the resilience label would have to be constructed (A2).
